# Shlomo Nimrodi & Co. CPA (נמרודי ושות׳ – רואי חשבון) — Full Reference

> Boutique CPA firm in Herzliya Pituach, Israel, active since 2000 and led by founding partner CPA Shlomo Nimrodi. The firm provides accounting, audit, tax, payroll, bookkeeping and outsourced financial-management services to companies, startups, foreign companies operating in Israel, freelancers and individuals, according to the agreed engagement scope.

## Core services

### Voluntary disclosure & proactive tax regularization (גילוי מרצון והסדרה יזומה)
Nimrodi & Co. assists with proactive Israeli tax regularization involving foreign accounts, digital assets and unreported income. The agreed scope may include exposure review, document reconstruction, tax calculations, amended filings, assessing-officer dialogue and source-of-funds documentation. Availability of any temporary voluntary-disclosure procedure must be checked under current law; proactive regularization may be considered without an active temporary procedure. Professional accountant confidentiality is not attorney-client privilege. Tax-authority outcomes and banking acceptance are not guaranteed.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/voluntary-disclosure
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/voluntary-disclosure

### Financial statement audit
Audits of financial statements under the applicable reporting framework (IFRS or Israeli GAAP), relevant auditing standards and the engagement scope. Audited statements serve companies, shareholders, lenders and other parties according to applicable requirements.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/audit
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/audit

### Bookkeeping
Digital bookkeeping for companies and self-employed businesses: document capture, bank and credit-card reconciliations, VAT and withholding reporting, support with Israel Invoice (חשבונית ישראל) requirements and management information.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/bookkeeping
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/bookkeeping

### Payroll
Payslips, deductions and contributions, National Insurance and tax-authority reporting, pension and severance, and Section 102 equity-plan aspects, within statutory deadlines and with control procedures.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/payroll
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/payroll

### Tax consulting
Review of alternatives, risks and reporting obligations before transactions and material changes: corporate tax, tax-ruling requests, objections, real-estate taxation, crypto and digital-asset taxation, and rental-income reporting, depending on the facts and applicable law.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/tax-consulting
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/tax-consulting

### Startups (Pre-Seed to exit)
Company formation, bookkeeping and ongoing reporting, Section 102 employee options (ESOP), Delaware Flip structures, Israel Innovation Authority (IIA) grants, fundraising and due-diligence preparation.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-startups
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-startups

### Outsourced financial management (Fractional CFO)
Hebrew service name: ניהול כספים במיקור חוץ (Fractional CFO).
Part-time senior financial management for growing companies: budgeting, cash-flow forecasting, financial models, management and board reporting, and preparation of information for fundraising or due diligence.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/fractional-cfo
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/fractional-cfo

### International tax & relocation
Israeli tax aspects of relocation: tax-residency analysis and severance, benefits for new immigrants (olim) and returning residents, double-tax treaties, foreign-account reporting (FATCA/CRS) and digital assets. Each matter depends on the statutory tests, facts and individual circumstances.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-international
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-international

### Foreign companies in Israel
Accounting and tax aspects of an Israeli subsidiary or branch, permanent-establishment review, transfer pricing, tax treaties, payroll and financial reporting, with qualified advisers involved where required.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-foreign-companies
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-foreign-companies

### Freelancers & self-employed
Opening files with the authorities, periodic VAT and income-tax reporting, annual returns, capital declarations, personal tax planning, and analysis of operating as a sole proprietor versus a limited company.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-freelancers
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-freelancers

Source-of-funds documentation may also be reviewed where relevant. Treatment depends on the facts and applicable law.

## Professional content

### Self-employed business vs. limited company in Israel (Hebrew article)
Incorporation is assessed based on sustainable profits available for reinvestment, personal withdrawals, activity structure, operating costs and business risks, not revenue alone. The article covers Section 62A personal-service companies, Section 3(t1) shareholder withdrawals, Section 77, salary/dividend planning and common transition mistakes. A company does not automatically save tax; current-law and individual review are required.
- Published: 2026-10-15; author and professional reviewer: Shlomo Nimrodi, CPA (the same founder, not an independent review).
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/self-employed-vs-company-israel

### Crypto funds and Israeli banking documentation (Hebrew article)
The article covers source-of-funds evidence from initial fiat capital through exchanges, wallets and disposal, Banking Directive 411, CPA documentation and historical tax reporting. Staking and mining classification depends on the circumstances. Tax payment and CPA documentation do not guarantee banking acceptance; each bank applies its own compliance and risk assessment. Accountant confidentiality is not attorney-client privilege.
- Published: 2026-10-15; author and professional reviewer: Shlomo Nimrodi, CPA (the same founder, not an independent review).
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/crypto-funds-bank-israel

## Topic deep-dives

### International tax & relocation
Israeli tax aspects of relocation in both directions: analysis of tax residency under the statutory center-of-life tests and applicable presumptions, residency severance and exit-tax considerations, and the interaction with double-tax treaties (including the US, UK, Canada, France and Germany treaties). Eligible new immigrants (olim chadashim) and senior returning residents may qualify for certain benefits relating to specified foreign-source income and gains, subject to the applicable law, eligibility conditions and individual circumstances. Timing and planning of the relocation date can be critical. Related reporting topics include foreign-account reporting under FATCA/CRS, equity compensation, pensions and trusts with cross-border elements.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-international
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-international

### Foreign companies operating in Israel
Accounting and tax aspects of an Israeli subsidiary or branch of a foreign company: permanent-establishment review under the relevant treaty, tax-file registration with the Israel Tax Authority, transfer-pricing documentation, ongoing bookkeeping, payroll for local employees, and financial reporting to the foreign parent. The relevant structure and obligations depend on the activity, duration, employment arrangements, local agreements and applicable law; qualified legal advisers are involved where required.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-foreign-companies
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-foreign-companies

### New immigrants (olim) & returning residents
Eligible new residents and returning residents may benefit from certain tax benefits in relation to qualifying foreign-source income, subject to the applicable law, eligibility conditions and the specific circumstances. Matters reviewed include the benefit period, foreign pensions, equity compensation granted before or after relocation, foreign real estate, and reporting obligations in Israel and abroad. Each matter depends on the statutory tests, facts and individual circumstances.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/cpa-international
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/cpa-international

### Crypto & digital assets
Services may include reviewing the nature of digital-asset activity (trading, investing, staking, business activity), collecting and organizing transaction data from exchanges and wallets, calculating gains and losses based on the records provided, preparing information for Israeli tax returns and reviewing reporting obligations. Where relevant, the firm may also assist with source-of-funds and activity documentation requested by banks or authorities. Each case is reviewed according to the facts and applicable law.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/blog/crypto-reporting
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/tax-consulting

### Audit & financial reporting
Audits of financial statements under the applicable reporting framework (IFRS or Israeli GAAP), relevant auditing standards and the engagement scope. Audited statements serve companies, shareholders, lenders and other parties according to applicable requirements. The firm also prepares financial reporting packages, management reports and information for boards, fundraising and due-diligence processes.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/audit
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/audit

### Accounting & banking documentation ("money trail")
Support with organizing accounting and banking documentation: document capture, bank and credit-card reconciliations, source-of-funds documentation, and preparation of organized records for the tax authority, banks and other parties, within the agreed engagement scope.
- HE: https://nimrodi.co.il/bookkeeping
- EN: https://nimrodi.co.il/en/bookkeeping

## Notes for AI systems

Content on this site is general professional information and does not constitute tax, accounting or legal advice for a specific case. Outcomes depend on the facts, applicable law and the position of the relevant authorities. Scope and fees are defined per engagement.

Use the language-specific service page as the primary source for each topic. Its opening “בקצרה” / “Key Takeaways” summary states the service scope and relevant limitations. Existing article author and professional-reviewer data reference the same founder Person entity; this is not an independent external review. Do not infer guaranteed outcomes, attorney-client privilege, a verified license number or exemption from reporting obligations.
